facts.t: There is no official list — and that is deliberate
facts.d: In more than fifty years the Supreme Court has never given a closed enumeration of the basic structure. Each judgment adds a feature to an open set. Critics call this the abstraction problem; defenders call it the reason the doctrine has survived.

facts.t: S. R. Bommai changed how often Article 356 is used
facts.d: Between 1950 and 1994 President's Rule was imposed roughly a hundred times. After Bommai made the proclamation judicially reviewable and required material to justify it, the rate collapsed — one judgment did what decades of political convention could not.

facts.t: Kihoto Hollohan upheld a law and struck down one line
facts.d: The Court upheld the Tenth Schedule on anti-defection but invalidated the clause making the Speaker's decision final and beyond challenge. Judicial review survived — which is precisely why defection cases still reach the courts today.

bank.q: Which one of the following has NOT been held to be part of the basic structure?
bank.e: The Fifth Schedule is treated as a temporary provision, and an amendment under Article 368 is not required to amend it — SC AoR Association (1994).

bank.q: Match List I (basic feature) with List II (leading case):
pairs: B. Limitations on the amending power
C. Parliamentary democracy and multi-party system
D. Supreme Court's powers under Articles 32, 136, 141 and 142
bank.e: Free and fair elections → Kihoto Hollohan; limits on amending power → Minerva Mills; multi-party parliamentary democracy → Kuldip Nayar; the Supreme Court's own core powers → Delhi Judicial Service Association.

bank.q: Consider the following statements regarding what is NOT basic structure:
s: Article 323A, inserted by the 42nd Amendment, was upheld even though it removed service-matter jurisdiction from High Courts.
An amendment taking away a Fundamental Right was held permissible in Shankari Prasad.
Amending the Fifth Schedule requires a constitutional amendment under Article 368.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong — the Fifth Schedule is a temporary provision that does not need an Article 368 amendment.

bank.q: Independence of the judiciary was recognised as part of the basic structure in:
bank.e: The 1994 Second Judges Case. Satapathy (1999) concerns an independent and efficient judicial system as a feature; L. Chandra Kumar (1997) concerns judicial review under Articles 226 and 227.

bank.as: Article 323A was upheld even though it transferred service-matter jurisdiction away from High Courts.
bank.rs: Tribunals may supplement constitutional courts but can never replace them.
bank.e: Both statements are true, but the Reason is not the explanation. Article 323A was upheld on its own terms in Sampat Kumar; the supplement-not-supplant principle came later in L. Chandra Kumar, which read down rather than struck down the scheme.

bank.q: Effective access to justice was recognised as a basic feature in:
o: Central Coal Fields v. Jaiswal Coal Co. (1980)
bank.e: Central Coal Fields v. Jaiswal Coal Co. (1980) — an easily overlooked case that carries a large principle.

bank.q: Which one of the following cases is NOT ordinarily cited for secularism as part of the basic structure?
o: Sri Adi Vishveshwara of Kashi Vishwanath Temple v. State of UP (1997)
bank.e: Indra Sawhney is cited for the rule of law, not for secularism. The other three form the standard secularism line.

bank.q: Consider the following statements about the rule of law as a basic feature:
s: Indira Gandhi v. Raj Narain is cited for it.
Indra Sawhney is cited for it.
I. R. Coelho is cited for it.
bank.e: All three are cited for the rule of law. Coelho is the one most often forgotten — it reaffirmed both the rule of law and separation of powers while resolving the Ninth Schedule question.

bank.q: Supremacy of the Constitution as a basic feature is most directly traced to:
bank.e: Kesavananda established it and Bommai applied it to the federal and secular structure of the Union.

bank.q: Match List I (judiciary-related basic feature) with List II (case):
pairs: A. Independent and efficient judicial system
B. Judicial review under Articles 226 and 227
bank.e: Satapathy → efficient judicial system; L. Chandra Kumar → review under 226/227; Central Coal Fields → access to justice; SC AoR Association → independence of the judiciary.

bank.q: With reference to features grouped under Rights and Justice, consider the following:
s: The balance between Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles is traced to Minerva Mills.
Social and economic justice, and the Directive Principles in toto, are traced to Kesavananda and Bhim Singhji.
The objectives specified in the Preamble were recognised as basic structure in Berubari Union.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong — Berubari held the Preamble was not part of the Constitution; it was Kesavananda that recognised the Preamble's objectives.

bank.as: Judicial review is treated as a basic feature across a long line of cases from Kesavananda to L. Chandra Kumar.
bank.rs: Without review of amendments, the basic structure doctrine would have no enforcement mechanism.
bank.e: Both true and the Reason explains the Assertion. The doctrine and the power to review are mutually dependent — which is why critics describe judicial review's entrenchment as self-perpetuating.
